'''Collette René Coullard''' is an American mathematician, [[industrial engineering|industrial engineer]], [[operations research]]er, and [[matroid]] theorist known for her research on [[combinatorial optimization]] problems that combine [[Optimal facility location|facility location]] and [[stock management]]. Formerly a professor at [[Purdue University]], the [[University of Waterloo]], [[Northwestern University]], and [[Lake Superior State University]], she has retired to become a [[professor emeritus]].

==Education and career==
Coullard graduated in 1980 from [[Lake Superior State University]],{{r|shouldice|deering}} and earned her Ph.D. in 1985 from [[Northwestern University]]. Her dissertation, ''Minors of 3-Connected Matroids and Adjoints of Binary Matroids'', concerned [[matroid theory]] and was supervised by [[Robert E. Bixby]].{{r|mgp}}

She taught at [[Purdue University]] and visited the [[University of Waterloo]]{{r|giden}} before returning to Northwestern as a faculty member in 1990,{{r|deering}} and retired as a mathematics professor from Lake Superior State University in 2018.{{r|ret}} She has also visited the [[University of Bonn]] as a [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Humboldt Fellow]].{{r|giden}}

==Recognition==
Coullard received the National Science Foundation Presidential Young Investigator Award in 1989.{{r|pyi}}  She was a Charles Deering McCormick Professor of Teaching Excellence at Northwestern University from 1996 to 1999.{{r|shouldice|deering}} In 2003, the Lake Superior State University Alumni Association gave her their annual Kenneth J. Shouldice Achievement Award.{{r|shouldice}}
